questions.stem: A 72-year-old man visits his physician because he finds it difficult to hold his hand steady when painting. Examination reveals a resting tremor and rigidity. The symptoms are relieved by a single dose of levodopa, suggestive of Parkinson’s disease. This patient’s neurological signs are most likely related to a lesion within which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: The cerebellum

options.label: B
options.text: The substantia nigra

options.label: C
options.text: The premotor area

options.label: D
options.text: The caudate nucleus and putamen

questions.solutionHtml:
The substantia nigra

Direct question: Parkinson’s Disease is caused by the destruction of the dopamine-secreting neurons within the substantia nigra of the basal ganglia.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology 14 Edition Page 736.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old boy is admitted to the hospital with a traumatic brain injury, sustained when he fell off his motorcycle. He develops a fever of 39°C, which is unrelated to an infection or inflammation. The fever is most likely due to a lesion of which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: The lateral hypothalamus

options.label: B
options.text: The arcuate nucleus

options.label: C
options.text: The posterior nucleus

options.label: D
options.text: The anterior hypothalamus

questions.solutionHtml:
The anterior hypothalamus

The anterior hypothalamus regulates body temperature.




Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 251–255.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrectly related to the hypothalamus?

options.label: A
options.text: A major part of the limbic system is the hypothalamus, with its related structures.

options.label: B
options.text: Control osmolality of the body fluids, and the drives to eat and drink.

options.label: C
options.text: Hypothalamus represents nearly 5% of the brain mass.

options.label: D
options.text: Large lateral hypothalamic area is present on each side of the hypothalamus.

questions.answerText: Hypothalamus represents nearly 5% of the brain mass.
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypothalamus represents nearly 5% of the brain mass.

Hypothalamus represents less than 1% of the brain mass and is the central element of the limbic system.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 744-746.

questions.stemHtml: Hypothalamus is a portion of the brain that contains a number of small nuclei. Hypothalamus links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland. An area marked in the red circle in the image located in the anterior portion of the hypothalamus has specific functions.Select the correct statements:-

options.label: A
options.text: Contains large numbers of heat-sensitive neurons and 1/3rd of cold-sensitive neurons.

options.label: B
options.text: Heat-sensitive neurons increase their firing rate 20 times in response to a 10°-C increase in body temperature.

options.label: C
options.text: Hypothalamic-preoptic area has the capability to serve as a thermostatic body temperature control center.

options.label: D
options.text: Only A and C correct

questions.solutionHtml:
Only A and C correct
  • Option A. Preoptic area contains large numbers of heat-sensitive neurons and 1/3rd of cold-sensitive
  • Option C. The hypothalamic-preoptic area has the capability to serve as a thermostatic body temperature control center.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology,14th Edition, Page No. 905-906.

questions.stem: Hypothalamus plays an active role in the release of all the other anterior pituitary hormones. Hypothalamus has been studied for the secretion of prolactin where the hypothalamus exhibits a specific type of action on the secretion of prolactin. Select the incorrect statements:

options.label: A
options.text: Hypothalamus mainly stimulates the production of all the other anterior pituitary hormones.

options.label: B
options.text: Damage to the hypothalamus or blockage of the hypothalamic-hypophyseal portal system elevates prolactin secretion.

options.label: C
options.text: Brain injury involving damage to the hypothalamus suppresses prolactin secretion.

options.label: D
options.text: Hypothalamus contains prolactin inhibitory hormone.

questions.answerText: Brain injury involving damage to the hypothalamus suppresses prolactin secretion.
questions.solutionHtml:
Brain injury involving damage to the hypothalamus suppresses prolactin secretion.

Brain injury involving damage to the hypothalamus increases prolactin secretion by blocking the hypothalamic-hypophyseal portal system and blocking the release of prolactin inhibitory hormone and increasing the release of prolactin.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 1057-1058.

questions.stemHtml: The image shown below represents a group of magnocellular neurosecretory cells located within the anterior hypothalamus that participate in the HPA axis.Select the best-suited statements:-

options.label: A
options.text: When the body fluids become highly diluted, neurons in these areas are stimulated.

options.label: B
options.text: Nerve endings secrete an antidiuretic hormone that regulates the amount of water in the body.

options.label: C
options.text: The hormone causes loss of water into the urine

options.label: D
options.text: Only B correct

questions.solutionHtml:
Only B correct

The nerve endings secrete an antidiuretic hormone that regulates the amount of water in the body.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.746.

questions.stemHtml: The ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH) is a distinct morphological nucleus involved in terminating fear, thermoregulation, and sexual activity. The ventromedial nuclei in the hypothalamus are depicted in the image as,Select the correct statements:

options.label: A
options.text: Damage to areas bilaterally causes lethal starvation.

options.label: B
options.text: This center opposes the desire for food.

options.label: C
options.text: Damage to areas bilaterally causes tremendous obesity.

options.label: D
options.text: Both B and C are correct

questions.answerText: Both B and C are correct
questions.solutionHtml:
Both B and C are correct
  • Option B. The ventromedial nuclei center opposes the desire for food.
  • Option C. Damage to ventromedial nuclei bilaterally causes tremendous obesity.
  • A center that opposes the desire for food, called the satiety center, is located in the ventromedial nuclei. When this center is stimulated electrically, an animal that is eating food suddenly stops eating and shows complete indifference to food. However, if this area is destroyed bilaterally, the animal cannot be satiated; instead, its hypothalamic hunger centers become overactive, so it has a voracious appetite, resulting eventually in tremendous obesity.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.746.

questions.stemHtml: The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) is a bilateral structure located in the anterior part of the hypothalamus. Its location is shown in the image given below:Select the best-suited functions:-

options.label: A
options.text: Serves as a “master clock” for many physiological, mental, and behavioral activities.

options.label: B
options.text: Receives direct innervation from the retina via the retinohypothalamic tract.

options.label: C
options.text: SCN neurons control various brain centers, which contain local circadian clocks.

options.label: D
options.text: All are best-suited functions

questions.solutionHtml:
All are best-suited functions
  • Option A. SCN serves as a “master clock” for many physiological, mental, and behavioral activities.
  • Option B. SCN receives direct innervation from the retina via the retinohypothalamic tract.
  • Option C. SCN neurons control various brain centers, which contain local circadian clocks.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.746-747.

questions.stem: A patient of age 34 years presented with symptoms of excessive drinking of water, excessive eating, sweating, anxiety, and occasional events of extreme rage on minor provocation. The patient gave a history of head injury in the previous year while riding a motorcycle. Examination and investigation revealed bilateral lesions in specific regions of the hypothalamus. Select the correct statement:

options.label: A
options.text: Bilateral lesions in ventromedial areas of the hypothalamus

options.label: B
options.text: Bilateral lesions in the lateral hypothalamus

options.label: C
options.text: Sometimes causes lethal starvation

options.label: D
options.text: Only A correct

questions.solutionHtml:
Only A correct

Bilateral lesions of the ventromedial areas of the hypothalamus cause effects that are mainly opposite to those caused by lesions of the lateral hypothalamus: excessive drinking and eating, as well as hyperactivity and often frequent bouts of extreme rage on the slightest provocation.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 748.

questions.stem: Synthesis of acetylcholine occurs in the presynaptic terminals. It is released into the synaptic cleft to act on the postsynaptic receptors. Select the irrelevant statements about parasympathetic postganglionic neurons:

options.label: A
options.text: Acetylcholine is synthesized by the action of choline-o-acetyltransferase on choline and acetyl coenzyme A.

options.label: B
options.text: The release of neurotransmitters is triggered when voltage-sensitive calcium channels open to allow the influx of calcium.

options.label: C
options.text: The released acetylcholine acts on postsynaptic nicotinic receptors.

options.label: D
options.text: Choline is recycled by being taken back up into the presynaptic terminal.

questions.answerText: The released acetylcholine acts on postsynaptic nicotinic receptors.
questions.solutionHtml:
The released acetylcholine acts on postsynaptic nicotinic receptors.

Acetylcholine activates mainly two types of receptors, which are called muscarinic and nicotinic receptors. The reason for these names is that muscarine, a poison from toadstools, activates only muscarinic receptors and will not activate nicotinic receptors, whereas nicotine activates only nicotinic receptors.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 766-67.

questions.stem: Psychotherapists studied the behavior of rats in a closed space. The rats were usually with normal behavior until there was one rat in one closed space. When many rats were enclosed in that space, they all turned on each other. Similarly, far more people on the road are responsible for road rage which must have been experienced by drivers in crowded places. Select the improper statements:

options.label: A
options.text: Signals are transmitted downward through the reticular formation of the brain stem and into the spinal cord to cause massive sympathetic discharge.

options.label: B
options.text: This is a sympathetic alarm reaction.

options.label: C
options.text: Reduced rate of blood coagulation, hyperperfusion of GIT and kidneys

options.label: D
options.text: Sympathetic stress response

questions.answerText: Reduced rate of blood coagulation, hyperperfusion of GIT and kidneys
questions.solutionHtml:
Reduced rate of blood coagulation, hyperperfusion of GIT and kidneys

When large portions of the sympathetic nervous system discharge at the same time—that is, a mass discharge— this action increases the ability of the body to perform vigorous muscle activity in many ways.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.766-67.

questions.stem: It is established that Signals from the hypothalamus and even from the cerebrum can affect the activities of almost all the brainstem autonomic control centers. Select the correct statement:

options.label: A
options.text: Stimulation in mainly of the posterior hypothalamus can activate the medullary cardiovascular control centers strongly enough to increase arterial pressure to more than twice normal.

options.label: B
options.text: The autonomic centers in the brain stem act as relay stations for control activities initiated at higher levels of the brain, especially in the hypothalamus.

options.label: C
options.text: Correct A and incorrect B

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and B correct

questions.solutionHtml:
Both A and B correct
  • Option A. Stimulation in mainly of the posterior hypothalamus can activate the medullary cardiovascular control centers strongly enough to increase arterial pressure to more than twice normal.
  • Option B. The autonomic centers in the brain stem act as relay stations for control activities initiated at higher levels of the brain, especially in the hypothalamus.
  • Signals from the hypothalamus and even from the cerebrum can affect the activities of almost all the brainstem autonomic control centers. For example, stimulation in appropriate areas—mainly of the posterior hypothalamus—can activate the medullary cardiovascular control centers strongly enough to increase arterial pressure to more than twice normal.
  • Likewise, other hypothalamic centers control body temperature, increase or decrease salivation and gastrointestinal activity, and cause bladder emptying. To some extent, the autonomic centers in the brain stem act as relay stations for control activities initiated at higher levels of the brain, especially in the hypothalamus.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No.774.

questions.stem: The parasympathetic nervous system predominates in quiet “rest and digest” conditions while the sympathetic nervous system drives the “fight or flight” response in stressful situations. The main purpose of the PNS is to conserve energy. The Parasympathetic System generally mediates specific Localized Responses in body organs. Select the correct statements:

options.label: A
options.text: Parasympathetic cardiovascular reflexes have a little direct effect on the myocardial force of contraction.

options.label: B
options.text: Salivary secretion can occur independently of gastric secretion but often occur simultaneously.

options.label: C
options.text: Parasympathetic cardiovascular reflexes act on the heart only to increase or decrease the heart rate.

options.label: D
options.text: All of them correct

questions.solutionHtml:
All of them correct

Control functions by the parasympathetic system are often highly specific. For example, parasympathetic cardiovascular reflexes usually act on the heart only to increase or decrease its rate of beating with a little direct effect on its force of contraction. Likewise, other parasympathetic reflexes cause secretion mainly by the mouth glands, and in other cases, secretion is mainly by the stomach glands. Finally, the rectal emptying reflex does not affect other parts of the bowel to a major extent.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 773-774.

questions.stem: In some cases, all portions of the sympathetic nervous system discharge simultaneously as a complete unit. Conversely, activation can occur in isolated portions of the sympathetic nervous system in other situations. Select the correct option for the activation of SNS in isolated portions:

options.label: A
options.text: Heating a skin area causes local vasodilation and enhanced local sweating.

options.label: B
options.text: Sympathetic control sweating and blood flow in the skin without affecting other organs.

options.label: C
options.text: Correct A and incorrect B

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and B correct

questions.solutionHtml:
Both A and B correct

In some cases, almost all portions of the sympathetic nervous system discharge simultaneously as a complete unit, a phenomenon called mass discharge. This frequently occurs when the hypothalamus is activated by fright or severe pain. The result is a widespread reaction throughout the body called the alarm or stress response, which is discussed shortly. At other times, the activation occurs in isolated portions of the sympathetic nervous system.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 773-774.

options.label: A
options.text: Lateral hypothalamic area

options.label: B
options.text: Perifornical region

options.label: C
options.text: The ventromedial nucleus of the hypothalamus

options.label: D
options.text: The dorsomedial nucleus of the hypothalamus

questions.answerText: The ventromedial nucleus of the hypothalamus
questions.solutionHtml:
The ventromedial nucleus of the hypothalamus
  • Hypothalamus controls appetite, satiety
  • Ventral posteromedial nucleus (VPN) of the hypothalamus: activates satiety
  • Lateral hypothalamic area: activates hunger, feeding



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 773-774

questions.stem: The thermoregulatory center is located at:

options.label: A
options.text: Pons

options.label: B
options.text: Hypothalamus

options.label: C
options.text: Medulla

options.label: D
options.text: Mid Brain

questions.solutionHtml:
Hypothalamus
  • The reflex responses activated by cold are controlled by the posterior hypothalamus. Those activated by warmth are controlled primarily by the anterior hypothalamus.
  • Stimulation of the anterior hypothalamus causes cutaneous vasodilation and sweating, and lesions in this region cause hyperthermia, with rectal temperatures sometimes reaching 43°C (109.4°F).
  • Posterior hypothalamic stimulation causes shivering, and the body temperature of animals with posterior hypothalamic lesions falls toward that of the environment.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 773-774

questions.stem: In damage to the Preoptic area in the hypothalamus:

options.label: A
options.text: Hypothermia

options.label: B
options.text: Hyperthermia

options.label: C
options.text: Loss of appetite

options.label: D
options.text: Increase appetite

questions.solutionHtml:
Hyperthermia

Damage to the median preoptic nucleus causes an elevated baseline body temperature.

Temperature homeostasis is regulated primarily in the preoptic area (POA) of the hypothalamus.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 916.

questions.stem: Appetite is stimulated by all of the following peptides, except:

options.label: A
options.text: Agouti - Related Peptide (AGRP)

options.label: B
options.text: Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH)

options.label: C
options.text: Melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH)

options.label: D
options.text: Neuropeptide Y

questions.solutionHtml:
Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH)

The melanocyte-stimulating hormone produced by the pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neuron is an MC4R agonist, and the agouti-related regulatory peptide (AgRP) is an inverse agonist of MC4R, and these antagonistically regulate appetite.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 890.
